label: Float-zone crystalline Si, Franta 2017/2018
specimen: Float-zone crystalline silicon; not polycrystalline or amorphous
source_kind: Author-provided tables of a dispersion model fitted to ellipsometry and spectrophotometry, not raw measurement points
caveat: The tabulated extension above about 143 um exceeds the 2017 paper measured band. CSV values are unchanged author-model spectra; the separate runtime BB extrapolation does not replace these source values.
temperature_caveat: Bundled numeric tables end at 500 K, despite the paper's broader experimental range. No values above 500 K have been fabricated.
name: Crystalline Si

sources.kind: Author-provided tables of a dispersion model fitted to ellipsometry and spectrophotometry, not raw measurement points

laser_rows: 1550 nm rows are linearly interpolated between the original neighboring wavelengths at each supplied temperature.
schema: temperature_k,wavelength_um,n,k; empty n or k means unknown
use: Benchmark BB_Franta uses the native 300, 350, 400, 450, 500 K spectra in a common 0.4–100 um integration band. The benchmark fits two temperature-scaling parameters to dipole powers at 350, 400, 450 K, with exact 300/500 K optical anchors and an explicit fixed Drude correction. The fitted dielectric function is extrapolated up to 1600 K; it is not additional Franta data. No room-optics reset above 500 K.
benchmark: The plot compares dipole and full Mie radiation using the same fitted hot optics, dipole and full Mie radiation with fixed 300 K optics, native Franta dipole points, and digitized Junnemann radiation. Hot Mie uses the same two-parameter extrapolation above 500 K without any extra fit. All calculated radiation curves share sphere geometry and bath temperature.
extrapolation_scope: The reduced fit is used only over 0.4–100 um; its UV continuation can become nonpassive. Code rejects negative imaginary permittivity rather than clipping it. The CSV itself retains its full original wavelength coverage.
